scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8876: host_1_1_1_1 (10.1.1.2) reports it cannot reach
anything outside its own subnet -- no server farm, no other pod, and name
lookups time out too. It can still ping its gateway address 10.1.1.1.
host_2_1_1_1 is unaffected and reaches everything normally. Diagnose
host_1_1_1_1's connectivity.

injection.action: point the host's default route at a non-existent in-subnet gateway
injection.command:
ip route del default 2>/dev/null
  ip route add default via 10.1.1.254

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: host_1_1_1_1 default-gateway configuration
Mechanism: host_1_1_1_1's correct gateway is 10.1.1.1 (switch_dist_1_1's br0
  address). Its default route was repointed to 10.1.1.254 -- in-subnet but
  unassigned -- so ARP for the gateway never resolves and no off-subnet
  packet leaves the host. On-link destinations (10.1.1.1 via the connected
  route) still work, which is why the gateway pings fine. DNS "times out"
  only because the resolver 10.200.0.2 is off-subnet. The network itself is
  healthy: pod 2 reaches everything, and switch_dist_1_1 still advertises
  10.1.1.0/24.
Localization: host_1_1_1_1
Root cause: host_1_1_1_1's default gateway set to 10.1.1.254 instead of
  10.1.1.1
Fix: restore the default route on host_1_1_1_1 --
  `ip route replace default via 10.1.1.1 dev eth0`
scenario.fix_spec:
restore host_1_1_1_1's default route --
`ip route replace default via 10.1.1.1 dev eth0`

bonus-exonerates-network: notes switch_dist_1_1 and the OSPF core are healthy (pod 2 works, the real gateway answers), so no network device needs fixing

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is a misconfigured default gateway on host_1_1_1_1. The host's
startup configuration sets its default route to 10.1.1.254 (`default via
10.1.1.254 dev eth0`), but no device in the 10.1.1.0/24 subnet owns that
address. The actual gateway — switch_dist_1_1's bridge interface br0 — is
configured with 10.1.1.1/24 (MAC d2:0e:bc:11:a7:c6), not 10.1.1.254.

Because 10.1.1.254 is reachable at Layer 2 only if something answers ARP for
it, and nothing does, every packet host_1_1_1_1 attempts to send beyond its
local /24 results in an unresolved ARP entry (visible as "(incomplete)" in the
host's ARP table). The kernel therefore immediately returns "Destination Host
Unreachable" for all off-subnet traffic — explaining why the host cannot reach
the server farm, other pods, or the DNS resolver (10.200.0.2). Meanwhile,
10.1.1.1 is within the same /24 and reachable via normal on-link ARP, which is
why the user can still ping the "gateway address" 10.1.1.1 directly — but that
address is never actually used for forwarding because the configured next-hop
is 10.1.1.254.

The faulty device is host_1_1_1_1 alone; switch_dist_1_1 and all upstream
routers are healthy and have correct OSPF routes.

Root cause: host_1_1_1_1's default gateway is set to 10.1.1.254 instead of
10.1.1.1.

Corrective fix: Change the default gateway on host_1_1_1_1 from 10.1.1.254 to
10.1.1.1 (i.e., `ip route replace default via 10.1.1.1 dev eth0` at runtime,
and update the startup script so the fix persists across restarts).

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly identifies host_1_1_1_1 as the faulty device and attributes the issue to a host-side default-gateway misconfiguration.
